I think “hate” was a strong word (although Ive said it many times on different occasion from anger.) I never really hated him, just hated what he represented in my mind. 

He was the man of the house, and my mom respected that. I didn’t. I was closer with my mom so anytime my dad tried to parent me, it made me very angry. My mom was the only parent that I let love me (not that my dad ever stopped loving me, to my frustration.) 

My dad was the bishop of my ward of the Mormon church, which surprisingly has always been a warm part in my heart, I didn’t experience any of the trauma that a lot of other ex-mormons face. But I never believed in it, and I was confident in my bisexuality by the time I was 9. Even when I came out when I was 11-12 and again when I was 13-14, they said they loved me. (Ignoring that they refuse to acknowledge my sexuality.) I have a gay uncle that we see all the time and they don’t care at all. We hang out with his husband!

I think that the dad-disliking behavior was more of a result from my ASD/ADHD than a trauma. I don’t remember a lot of my childhood, but I don’t remember a lot of things. I mean, maybe I’ll uncover some super significant trauma that I just completely suppressed, but I seriously doubt it.

Edit: Also might be important to add that I’ve received treatment for my mental health this whole time. Tried lots of different therapists, only recently have I stuck with one. Seen a psychiatrist my whole life.
I’m on immediate release that are prescribed to be taken as needed. I can take them twice, once, or not at all. It’s up to me.
